name: CA-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about eight points and Harder is the incumbent
Overwhelming money advantage: roughly $4.7 million on hand for Harder versus about $19,000 for McBride
Prediction markets price Harder's reelection at 97-98 percent
No public general-election polling, so the outlook rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's Democratic lean, Harder's incumbency, and his enormous fundraising edge all point the same direction, and markets on Kalshi and Polymarket price his reelection near certainty. With no public polls and almost no outside spending against him, nothing in the evidence justifies moving away from a roughly twenty-point Democratic margin.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Harder or an unusually favorable Republican turnout environment could narrow what is otherwise a lopsided financial and structural picture.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Josh Harder, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Central Valley district that leans Democratic by about eight points. He holds a decisive financial edge, having raised more than $4 million and reporting roughly $4.7 million on hand, while Republican John McBride has raised about $52,000. Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket put Harder's chances at 97 to 98 percent.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on the district's partisan lean, Harder's incumbency, and the spending gap. Outside spending in the race has been negligible, and there are no expert ratings flagging vulnerability. The contest is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty coming from turnout in a low-profile race rather than any documented shift in candidate strength.
